title: getting-started tells the reader st edit design works, and it refuses on both binaries because design is not a member of a v3 thread
body:
**`docs/getting-started.md:64` tells the reader that `$EDITOR "$(intent st edit ST0001 design)"` behaves as they expect. It does not, on either binary.**

Driven from an empty directory, twice, following the page literally:

    intent st edit ST0001 design
    error: `intent/st/ST0001/design.md` is not a file this artefact carries
      remedy: this artefact carries: acceptance.md, info.md

Identical on the published keg `intent 3.0.0 (80d8b2ca)` and on the tree `intent 3.0.0 (a854d7c3)`. **It is not a keg-lag defect** -- both builds refuse, so it does not resolve at the tag.

**Creating the file first does not help, which is the part that identifies the subject.** With `design.md` present on disk the refusal is unchanged, and the remedy's list grows to `WP/01/info.md, WP/02/info.md, acceptance.md, info.md` -- so the file set is read from the ARTEFACT MODEL, not from the directory. `design` is not a member of a v3 thread, and `st new` lays down `acceptance.md` and `info.md` only. The verb is correct and its remedy is honest; the page is what is wrong.

=== THE PART THAT IS NOT JUST A WRONG SENTENCE ===

**`intent search --help` says `Full-text search across all authored prose`, and `search_surface.rs:81` names `design.md`, `impl.md` and `tasks.md` as Source 1 of that prose.** So one subsystem treats these files as first-class authored content while another denies they belong to the artefact at all. Driven: a `design.md` containing a distinctive phrase returns no hit for that phrase, while a term in the canon objective returns hits.

That makes the page's claim a symptom rather than the defect. **Two subsystems hold different answers to "what files does a thread have", which is the two-homes shape Intent exists to prevent, in Intent.** Whichever answer is right, one of them needs to change, and the page should be corrected to whichever survives.

=== WHAT WAS FIXED NOW ===

The single false sentence at `:64`, because the page's opening claim is that every command on it has been run. The `search`-versus-model disagreement is left for whoever owns the model; it is named here so the page is not corrected twice.
